reagents.name: FGF4
reagents.identity_limit: No catalog, construct, lot, stock carrier or vehicle specified. Distinct from FGF2/bFGF.

current_research_listing.identity: Human recombinant FGF4, E. coli-expressed 177-aa approximately 19-kDa protein

reagents.name: AA, as reported for late exposure
reagents.timing: Days 5–15, alone or with FGF4 10 ng/mL
reagents.form_qualification: Methods explicitly name L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate sesquimagnesium salt hydrate (Sigma) in early RPMI/BSA medium. outcomes.positive: FGF4 alone raises cTnT/cTnI/MLC2v/MLC2a/ANP. AA alone raises MLC2v/MLC2a/ANP. Combination markedly increases MLC2v (~35-fold vs control) and exceeds FGF4 alone.
outcomes.component_limit: No formal factorial interaction established; combination gain not individually assigned to each reagent.

outcomes.positive: cTnT/MLC2v and alpha-actinin/MLC2v staining after FGF4 and combination; MLC2a also present.
outcomes.limit: No quantified adult ventricular purity; authors acknowledge incomplete maturation.

outcomes.positive: Combination shows more synchronous/regular spontaneous beating traces and shorter, less dispersed peak-to-peak intervals.
outcomes.method: 50-fps microscopy; regional light-intensity change over 10 s
outcomes.reported_test: Two-tailed unpaired t-test, P<0.001 for pooled intervals
outcomes.unit_limit: Not established independent biological replicates; possible region/interval clustering. P is not a separate test of synchrony or variance.

outcomes.positive_for_modeling: Combination-pretreated cells release more cTnI, CK-MB and myoglobin under hypoxia at differentiation days 17,19,21; plotted comparisons carry P<0.05 or P<0.01 versus concurrent normoxia.
outcomes.exposure: Nominal 2% versus 21% O2 after washout, days 15–21; 24-h collection wording not fully aligned with continuous schedule.
outcomes.limit: No cell-number/viability normalization; altered marker content may contribute.

outcomes.observation: Acute fall after day 15 with rate recovery toward baseline by differentiation day 25; peak-to-peak remains annotated significant at day 25.
outcomes.limit: No demonstrated drug rescue or survival fraction; unit and repeated-measure structure unclear.

outcomes.observation: Hypoxia-associated cleaved-caspase-3 staining and morphological membrane damage.
outcomes.limit: Qualitative images without quantitative survival assay; not a reagent toxicity test.

bub1b.measurement: BUB1B transcript, RNA-seq and qRT-PCR; interaction network derived from STRING
bub1b.contrast: 24-h hypoxia versus normoxia after both groups received FGF4 + AA on days 5–15
bub1b.qpcr_replication: Triplicate data using the same RNA samples as RNA-seq; not independent biological validation

reporting_issues.observations: Methods 2 µM versus Figures S1/S4 5 µM.
Reported 2% O2 + 94% N2 + 5% CO2 sums to 101%.
Reported hypoxia injury fold changes match rounded S5 hypoxia-arm day-15 baseline ratios rather than consistently concurrent normoxia.
reporting_issues.handling: Retain raw reported means and plotted significance/direction; do not label quoted ratios as concurrent normoxia comparisons.

reporting_issues.observations: Results claim day-19 increase; Figure 3/S5 instead show 0.004 ng/mL hypoxia versus 0.085 normoxia.
Main text says recovery over next 17 days; Figure S8 shows differentiation days 15–25.

unestablished: FGF4 or AA monotherapy functional superiority
BUBR1 protein abundance, stability or acetylation rescue
quantitative survival or dose-dependent reagent toxicity
fair_comparison: Preserve the specific cardiac differentiation and optical function positives. Niacin and apitegromab remain provisional and MVA-unproved; this experiment cannot rank clinical MVA efficacy or justify replacement. Hypoxia injury does not establish intrinsic reagent harm.

integration_status: Integrated as original assessment; raw source materials remain outside Git; no additional abstract credit.

report.scope: Independent comparison of appraisal.md and evidence.json with complete saved primary Methods, main Figures 2 and 3 and their legends, Figure 5 legend, supplementary Figure S10 and its legend, the BUB1B primer row, and GEO series plus both sample metadata records.

checks.finding: Early medium explicitly contains L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate sesquimagnesium salt hydrate from Sigma. The late day-5–15 intervention is called AA at 200 µg/mL without a separately specified chemical form or catalog. The appraisal correctly qualifies phosphate-context mapping and does not authenticate late AA as plain ascorbic acid or a particular phosphate product.

Main combination is FGF4 10 ng/mL plus AA 200 µg/mL during days 5–15. FGF2 10 ng/mL is a distinct comparator. Figure 2 compares untreated cultures with the combination; it does not resolve the individual functional contributions of FGF4 and AA.

The method records regional light-intensity variation at 50 frames/s over 10 s. The figure supports more regular/synchronous contraction traces and shorter, less dispersed peak-to-peak intervals. Its n=63 and n=80 and unpaired two-tailed t-test P<0.001 are not established counts of independent cultures. The appraisal correctly avoids force, electrophysiology or independently tested synchrony/variance claims.

sources: GEO series and both sample records
checks.finding: Figure S10B prints BUB1B RNA-seq 0.3 and qRT-PCR 0.5 relative expression. Both normoxia and 24-h hypoxia samples were pretreated with FGF4+AA. This is a transcript decrease under the hypoxia contrast, not a measured effect of adding FGF4+AA versus untreated cells or BUBR1 restoration. The qPCR legend says the same RNA samples and triplicate data.

The series lists two deposited sample records, one normoxia and one hypoxia. Upstream pooling is not described. These records do not establish independent biological replication for the RNA-seq contrast; triplicate qPCR from the same samples is not independent biological validation.

sources: GEO series summary and overall design
checks.finding: The source exposes pretreated cells to hypoxia after washing. Figure 3 shows greater injury-marker release in the combination-pretreated hypoxia arm than concurrent normoxia on days 17, 19 and 21. This supports the injury-model interpretation and does not establish hypoxia protection, a drug rescue, or intrinsic reagent toxicity. The stated gas percentages total 101%, as the appraisal already flags.

unresolved_questions: Chemical form/catalog/lot of the late AA exposure.
Independent culture/differentiation units and clustering underlying optical n=63/80.
Upstream sample pooling and biological replication for RNA-seq/qPCR.
